verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev tasks are plain code kept in your own repo. A documented GitHub Action deploys tasks when code is pushed to main, and the platform has separate environments and preview branches with environment-scoped API keys, so source-control versioning and environment-targeted deploys are supported. However, no evidence shows a first-class promotion step that moves a tested version from dev or staging into production; teams appear to redeploy per environment instead. missing for 10: an explicit dev-to-production promotion workflow, documentation of deployment version history and rollback, and independent hands-on corroboration of multi-environment promotion.

support.subject: As a developer, I can version workflows through source control or environments and promote changes from dev to production

citations.quote: This simple GitHub action workflow will deploy your Trigger.dev tasks when new code is pushed to the `main` branch.
If a single process needs to talk to more than one Trigger.dev project, environment, or preview branch, use `new TriggerClient({...})` for each target instead of `configure()`.
using a named API key associated with a specific environment in a project (`secretKey`)
Define prompt templates as code, version them on deploy
making changes my workflows in IDE takes about 80% less time
